lockup.summary: Existing holders are released in steps. The first group can sell 35 days after the prospectus date, and all remaining shares can be sold by day 181. Some shares can be released sooner if the stock price rises well above the IPO price.

what: Oura makes the Oura Ring, a smart ring, and a paid membership app that tracks sleep, activity and other health signals.
proceeds: Oura expects about $532.6 million in net proceeds, and about $526.4 million of it will go to tax payments tied to employee stock units vesting at the IPO. The rest is for general business costs such as technology development, working capital, operating expenses and equipment.
risks: Oura's fast revenue growth may not last, and growth is expected to slow over time.
If Oura cannot attract new members or keep existing ones paying, its business and growth will suffer.
Oura faces strong competition from larger companies with more money, bigger brands and wider sales reach.
Oura has only recently become profitable and may not stay profitable as its costs rise.
If Oura cannot keep launching new and improved products and features, its sales and growth could suffer.
